learning_items: The selected production UI stack is React, TypeScript, Vite, and Tauri 2 for shared Web, macOS, and Windows behavior; PySide6 is not the product frontend.
Remote CI billing failure is external provenance, not product execution evidence; successful local native acceptance may close the product gate when the user explicitly selects local authority.
Desktop acceptance must verify target-native sidecar and installer architecture, installed-app interaction, credential stripping, and outbound socket blocking.
Responsive-hidden controls still require keyboard-accessible user paths and stable DOM selectors in native WebView acceptance.
The renderer-neutral preview must remain explicit that it is not exact Word pagination.

promoted_checks.statement: Desktop release verification must reject a managed sidecar or installer whose executable architecture does not match the declared native target.
When responsive CSS hides a secondary action, acceptance must prove that the documented keyboard path still performs the same user operation.
